question: With packing, facts, per-row need labels, unique input count, initial weights and updates matched, does exposing compound records under partial observation improve need decisions over format exposure alone?
data_scope: Literal spans from pinned Mem2Act user passages. Controlled requests and observations. Atomic versus compound concatenations conserve the same two facts. Minimal banks, not a retrieval competition or live tool benchmark.
partition: Reuse the original train/dev/test source partition. Test source groups remain absent from training, but their results have already been inspected; this is a mechanism diagnostic, not fresh confirmation.
labels: goal_link = supplies a requested attribute regardless of current observations; needed_now = supplies a requested attribute not already confirmed. Explicit coverage and source spans are audited separately. Actual worker effects never replace these labels.
states: Eight frozen requested/observed attribute combinations, each paired across atomic and compound packing.

training.lora: continue rank8 q/v from prior single for the same seed
training.loss: Unchanged parent need-only weighted cross entropy; 400 state entries, batch 4, 200 updates. Format/relation have identical per-row candidate labels and therefore identical loss weights. Repeat retains the original atomic replay data.

selection: Primary fixed threshold 0.5. No threshold, checkpoint, arm or seed selected on evaluation outcomes.
evaluation: Reuse all 384 prior test states as a previously observed diagnostic. Primary 48 partly observed compound states; also all states, atomic controls and old BEAM development regression. Score all models after training and freeze their hashes first.

worker.task: Recover requested fields as a JSON object; never execute an external tool.

worker_policy: Reuse exact-message-hash cached Qwen3.5-4B outputs for all 96 compound/prose states. Missing cache entries stop evaluation; no new worker calls.
resource_rule: One local GPU process at a time, require native BF16 and >=10GiB free before loading; never interrupt another user's process. Exit after bounded work and preserve incomplete status on failure.
reporting: Primary contrast is relation minus format. Repeat is an additional descriptive reference, with fewer unique inputs and a different packing distribution. Form/rel have identical banks, requested facts, per-row need/goal labels and common atomic/anchor rows. Observation information differs by design in 80 rows; selector text length is not exactly matched. No general retrieval superiority or fresh-source confirmation claim.
baseline_note: With at most two records, dense_top2 and any unfiltered top2 equal budget_fill. No separate dense inference needed; this equality does not support a retrieval superiority claim.

primary_contrast.direction: Report both seeds and every stratum, regardless of direction; no outcome-dependent extension.
